## portcheck scan

Check which TCP ports are reachable on remote hosts

### Synopsis

Check which TCP ports accept connections on remote hosts.

portcheck makes ordinary TCP connections, so it needs no special privileges.
It has no stealth or evasion features. Each port is reported as:

  open      a connection was established
  closed    the host refused the connection
  filtered  no answer before --timeout (often a firewall)
  error     another failure, e.g. no route to host

Only scan hosts and networks you own or are authorized to test.

Exit status is 0 if any port is open and 1 if none are.

```
portcheck scan <host|ip|cidr>... [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  portcheck scan db.internal -p 5432
  portcheck scan 10.0.0.0/28 -p 22,80,443 --open
  portcheck scan example.com -p well-known --rate 100 --json
```

### Options

```
      --concurrency int    simultaneous connection attempts (default 100)
  -h, --help               help for scan
      --max-hosts int      refuse to scan more hosts than this (default 1024)
      --open               only show open ports
  -p, --ports string       ports to scan, e.g. 22,80,8000-8100 or a preset (common, well-known, ...) (default "common")
      --rate float         maximum new connections per second (0 = unlimited) (default 500)
      --retries int        extra attempts for ports that time out
      --timeout duration   per-connection timeout (default 1s)
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --json                shorthand for --output json
      --log-format string   log format: text or json (default "text")
      --no-color            disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR)
  -o, --output string       output format: table, plain, csv, json (default: table on a terminal, plain otherwise)
  -v, --verbose             log diagnostic details to stderr
```
